The test image shows soybean pods - one split open revealing pale/cream round seeds, with dark discoloration at the pod tip. This looks like a pod/seed disease. Top candidates: Phomopsis (chalky white seeds), Charcoal_Rot, Anthracnose (pod lesions with dark tips), Fusarium.

Now I'll view one reference from each of 16 classes, starting with the most likely candidates.

Now I have my 16 reference images across 16 classes. Let me analyze the test image against what I've seen.

**Test image summary:** Soybean pods hanging from plant, one pod split open revealing 2-3 pale/cream round plump seeds. Dark discoloration at pod tip. Brownish-tan mature pod with typical fine hairs.

**Key comparison:**
- **Purple_Seed_Stain** (Soybean_Dise_4): closest match — opened pod showing pale/cream seeds, same pod appearance and split scenario
- **Phomopsis** (Soybean_Dise_14): seeds were shriveled/rotten, not plump like test image
- **Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus** (Soybean_Dise_10): opened pod with seeds, but seeds had dark mottling — not matching
- All leaf-disease classes (Bacterial_Blight, Septoria, Frogeye, etc.): clearly wrong context (no pods/seeds)

The test image seeds are plump and round (not shriveled), pale/cream colored — consistent with Purple_Seed_Stain where disease causes color changes but seeds remain full-sized. The pod-split scenario closely mirrors the Purple_Seed_Stain reference.
